item.title: Jaguars offense gets an F for a sloppy, clunky effort in loss to Giants
item.description: Grading the Jacksonville Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the New York Giants on Nov. 22 in East Rutherford, N.J. The Jaguars (7-3) will return home after three road games in a row to host the Tennessee Titans on Nov. 29 at EverBank Stadium. Offense: F Yuck. Start with nine offensive penalties, including four false starts by four players. There was an illegal formation, an illegal shift, a delay penalty and quarterback Trevor Lawrence came through with an oldie, but never a goodie, throwing a pass beyond the line of scrimmage ... and it wasn't close. Lawrence had three interceptions if you count the one on a two-point conversion attempt (it's not) and many of his incompletions were high. He was sacked three times and was hit eight other times. The running game struggled because the Giants' defensive line overpowered the Jags offensive line. It was a basic as football gets. The Jaguars scored only one touchdown in six trips to the red zone against a defense that had given up touchdowns on 80 percent of their oppositions' trips inside the 20-yard line. What else? How about 5 of 15 on third down (failing to convert on their first seven when it was third-and-eight or longer) and failing to punch the ball in after two shots with 2 yards to go in the third quarter? It was a mess. Defense: B This was a borderline A until the Giants' last possession, when the Jags absolutely, positively had to get the ball back with 3:40 left in the game and only one time out left. But J.J. McCarthy his Malachi Fields for 19 yards and Cam Skattebo ran for two 5-yard gains to give the Giants a first down at the two-minute warning, enabling the victory formation. Also detracting from the final grade was losing contain on McCarthy, who had a 22-yard scramble on third-and-five and a 13-yard gain on third-and-eight. He had another 29-yard run nullified by a penalty. Other than that, the Jaguars' defense played well enough to give the offense a chance. The Jaguars failed to score after Antonio Harrison's 42-yard fumble return and a missed 32-yard field goal by Dominic Zvada. Josh Hines-Allen had his first solo sack since the opening game of the season but McCarthy got hit only three other times. Skattebo was no factor until the final possession (14 carries, 34 yards, 2.4 yards per attempt) and McCarthy threw some terrible passes, with a final rating of 69.3. Malik Nabers got a TD pass but was otherwise invisible and tight end Isaiah Likely caught only one pass. It was a big one, 35 yards, but went for naught when Zavada hooked his field-goal attempt. Special teams: C For the third game in a row, Cam Little made all four of his field goal attempts, and he's made 18 in a row and 22 of 24 this season. Ameer Abdullah gave the Jaguars great field position with a 47-yard return of the opening kickoff but after getting a first down to the Giants' 14, the offense stalled and Little kicked his first field goal. item.title: Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol after Chargers’ Week 11 loss to Jets
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol after Chargers’ Week 11 loss to Jets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers were sent crashing back to earth after losing to the New York Jets, 27-24 , at SoFi Stadium on Sunday. All the high from the Chargers’ win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 10 was erased, and it could be more costly, as Herbert was placed in concussion protocol. He played the entire game without exiting for a sideline evaluation. The Chargers have not specified the exact play on which he got hurt. The 28-year-old quarterback did not face the media , as noted by KTLA’s Hayley Elwood. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Justin Herbert is in the concussion protocol per Chargers PR. He will not be speaking postgame,” wrote Elwood on X. Herbert absorbed significant punishment against the Jets, taking six sacks and eight hits. He suffered a smack to the facemask from David Bailey in the second quarter, which drew a roughing-the-passer call. The two-time Pro Bowler threw 15-of-21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns. He also scored on a short rush to end the first half. The Chargers remained winless at home and fell to 1-9. The Jets, meanwhile, broke their five-game losing streak to the Chargers and improved to 3-8. The much-hyped pairing of Herbert and Mike McDaniel has not worked, and Los Angeles is in danger of missing the playoffs for the second time in four years. If Herbert is unable to clear the concussion protocol before Week 12 against the New England Patriots, DJ Uiagalelei is next in line to start, with Trey Lance out with a groin injury and Jake Browning on the practice squad. item.title: Pierre LeBrun Reveals Stunning Dylan Larkin Trade Secret Kept Quiet for Months
item.description: The Dylan Larkin trade saga finally came to an end Sunday night when the Detroit Red Wings sent their former captain to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster deal. But according to NHL insider Pierre LeBrun , there was a major secret being kept behind the scenes for months. And it changes the way we look at how this entire situation unfolded. Following the trade, LeBrun revealed that Larkin had actually been willing to accept a move to Montreal for more than two months. However, the Canadiens and Larkin’s representatives reportedly agreed to keep that information quiet. “So, it turns out Dylan Larkin was actually open to a trade to Montreal for more than two months,” LeBrun wrote on X, according to the post provided. “But the Canadiens wanted to keep that quiet because they felt it would add an extra layer of noise that might hamper getting a deal done. And Larkin’s camp agreed.” That’s a fascinating revelation considering the months of speculation surrounding Larkin’s approved trade destinations. Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Michael Hage Was the Key to Getting the Deal Done According to LeBrun, Montreal had been a legitimate possibility much longer than the public realized. However, the Canadiens still had to satisfy Detroit’s asking price, which reportedly included one particularly important asset. Michael Hage. “Montreal agreeing to include Hage was a huge must for the Red Wings,” LeBrun reported. “The deal started to come together and get serious on Friday.” That detail is especially interesting considering Hage had previously emerged as a potential centerpiece in a hypothetical deal between the two organizations. Now, we know just how important the 20-year-old University of Michigan standout was to Detroit’s negotiations. According to the NHL’s official trade announcement , the Red Wings received Hage, Kirby Dach, Samuel Montembeault, two conditional first-round picks, a second-round selection, and a fourth-round pick. Montreal received Larkin, along with Detroit’s 2027 third-round and 2028 second-round selections. item.title: Dylan Larkin traded to Montreal Canadiens for goalie, package of picks
item.description: The divorce between the Detroit Red Wings and disgruntled former captain Dylan Larkin is finally complete. Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff traded Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday, Nov. 22, acquiring forwards Kirby Dach, Michigan Wolverines prospect Michael Hage, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 and a second round pick in 2028 and a fourth-round pick in 2028. Larkin is in Year 4 of an eight-year deal carrying an $8.7 million salary cap hit that is highly favorable in a league where the 2026-27 salary cap ceiling is $104 million. Larkin, 30, signed an eight-year, $69.6 million extension with the Wings on March 1, 2023. DYLAN BUCKS: Larkin tops $1 million forfeited while awaiting Red Wings trade Larkin had two goals and four assists in 10 games for the Wings this season, before leaving the team on Oct. 29. The Wings suspended Larkin without pay that same day , costing him $41,237.11 a day. Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, told reporters, "Dylan’s had enough of the situation." Sunday monrig marked more than $1 million of salary forfeited back to the team. Larkin's final goal in a Wings uniform came Oct. 26, tying the game late in the third period at Edmonton in an eventual thrilling shootout win. He didn't play again. LARKIN LATE TYING GOAL 🚨 Red Wings applying massive pressure with the empty net - Seider finds Raymond who gets it to Larkin for the game tying tally. Detroit sends it to overtime. #LGRW pic.twitter.com/yCVN8muhU7 — Ryan Hana (@RyanHanaWWP) October 27, 2026 Larkin was soundly booed by his hometown fans when he was introduced during opening night Oct. 2 at Little Caesars Arena while out with an upper-body injury sustained in the offseason . Larkin was again booed in his season debut Oct. 6 after missing the season's first two games, but turned jeers to cheers after scoring a goal and being named the game's first star. Montreal fans at Bell Centre chanted "We want Larkin!" on Oct. 10, the most notable away crowd reaction to the saga. News broke on June 4 that Larkin, who had a no-trade clause, had requested a trade after 11 seasons with his hometown Wings. Larkin is from nearby Waterford, attended the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor and had been the Wings' captain until he was stripped of the title after the trade request became public. Larkin has gone 10 years without appearing in the NHL playoffs – the Wings own the NHL's longest playoff drought – and his gold-medal success at the 2026 Milano Olympics likely reminded him how fun it is to win important games. He returned to Detroit from that experience, and watched as a Wings team that had been 10 points inside the playoff picture in late January lost its foothold and dropped out of contention, again. Steve Yzerman, removed as GM in July , said shortly after the season he received a phone call from Larkin's agent informing him Larkin wanted to be traded. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was disqualified in the third quarter of Sunday’s 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles after drawing his second personal foul of the game. item.description: Some Cal football fans have had enough. Following the Golden Bears’ rough 44-28 loss in the “Big Game” to their cross-bay rivals Stanford, falling to 3-8 on the season, fans were caught on video cursing out players as they left the field. It’s never good when opposing fans rush the field in your home stadium. But that’s not an excuse for fans cussing out college football players and putting it on the internet. California Golden Bears head coach Tosh Lupoi looks on against the Stanford Cardinal in Berkeley, Calif., Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Getty Images But that’s where the Golden Bears find themselves while head coach Tosh Lupoi faces real questions about his job security as an embarrassing season winds down. But Cal hasn’t been competitive for over a month. They haven’t won since knocking off Virginia Tech on Oct. 10, and have lost by an average of 26.2 points over their ongoing five-game losing streak. They’ll look to snap it in their season finale next week when they host Pittsburgh. item.title: Player grades: SGA-less Thunder punt in 123-113 loss to Heat
item.description: Eventually scratched from his first game of the season, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's absence turned this into a skippable watch at worst and background noise at best. The two-time MVP winner went through his pregame warmups, but that was it in his sole visit to one of the most historic gyms in the NBA. The Oklahoma City Thunder stomached through a 123-113 loss to the Miami Heat . They trailed the entire night and by as many as 20 points. Before the cross-conference matchup even happened, the Thunder punted it on the front end of road back-to-back. Not only was Gilgeous-Alexander, but so were Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Cason Wallace, Alex Caruso and plenty of other names. To twist the knife, Aday Mara was a very-late scratch, too. Sure, the Heat were without Giannis Antetokounmpo, but it was a matchup of their B squad butting heads with OKC's C squad. The only Opening Night starter who was suited up for the Thunder was Isaiah Hartenstein. This is the NBA reality they're in right now with their long list of injuries. Any hopes of a miraculous win popped like a balloon. Not even three minutes in, the Thunder were in an 11-2 deficit. Klay Thompson grilled them from the outside — ala 2016. Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain tried their best collective carry job, but just didn't have the scoring superpowers to do so. The Thunder were in a 36-24 deficit after the first quarter. Finally, the Thunder enjoyed some outside shooting luck. Kenrich Williams drained a 3-pointer to make it a single-digit contest. But anytime it felt like OKC was about to go on a run, the Heat answered back with timely outside jumpers. That was the game's flow throughout the first half. The Thunder had 30 points in the second quarter. They entered halftime with a 67-54 deficit. Bam Adebayo balled out as he flirted with a triple-double. It was the first time this year that he enjoyed first-option hoops. Alas, the second half brought zero intrigue. It was mostly the same as both teams played it out of necessity. Williams had some nice scoring plays, but made costly mistakes as he was asked to be one of their top players. Josh Dix also showed flashes as OKC's best two-way guy with outside makes and good defensive energy. Mitchell had an epic four-point play. But yeah, that's really it. We're really grasping at straws to find meaty thoughts on this inevitable loss once Gilgeous-Alexander was ruled out. The Thunder had 26 points in the third quarter, but the Heat continued to stiff-arm them on the scoreboard. At that juncture in the game, OKC was in a 95-80 hole. Remember when it had a several-year run as one of the league's top defenses? If you stayed through this, you're a real NBA trooper. Enjoy whatever online brownie points you can get. The skeleton Thunder gave you every incentive to tune into the NFL Sunday slate instead. The fourth quarter was forgettable as the game got out of hand. OKC put up 33 points in the final frame to pretty up the final score of this wire-to-wire defeat.

item.title: Ravens Star Silenced for Joke, Even as Team’s Season Collapses
item.description: Jul 29, 2026; Ownings Mills, MD, USA; Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey (44) during practice at the Under Armour Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images Marlon Humphrey made a joke on his own podcast. Asked what Baltimore is best at making, he named the Star-Spangled Banner and National Bohemian beer, then added, “They’re best at making criminals.” It was a throwaway line in a casual conversation. He immediately noted it would get cut. The next day, he apologized, pointing out that he’s spent his whole career in the city, has welcomed a son there, and invests locally. The Ravens treated it like a major offense. Coach Jesse Minter sent him home from the facility and made him a healthy scratch for Sunday’s game against the Panthers. One-game deactivation, still gets paid, conversations “personal and private.” Officially it’s about removing a distraction while the team tries to snap a five-game losing streak. That framing doesn’t hold up. The Ravens are 4-6 and sliding. They’re already missing other defensive starters. Humphrey has started every game this season and is the longest-tenured defensive player on the roster. His recent play has been inconsistent, yet the organization has kept him in the lineup and at the top of the cornerback pay scale. A light podcast joke produced an immediate benching . The actual losses have not. Mayor Brandon Scott and others called the comment unacceptable and the apology insufficient. Public criticism is part of the job. What’s harder to defend is a struggling franchise choosing this moment for a public stand. When a team is getting beaten week after week, deactivating a starter over an offhand remark looks more like virtue signaling than football discipline. It signals seriousness without fixing the problems that actually cost games. Humphrey is expected back next week. The Ravens’ larger issues—offensive inconsistency, defensive holes, a losing streak—will still be there. Silencing a player for a joke doesn’t change any of that. It just gives a flailing organization something to point to while the losses continue.

item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Red Wings have finally said enough is enough. Six months after Dylan Larkin requested a trade out of Detroit, interim general manager Shawn Horcoff has granted the former Red Wings captain’s request. Larkin is going to the Montreal Canadiens alongside a 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round selection from the Red Wings in exchange for goaltender Sam Montembault, forward Kirby Dach, and top prospect center Michael Hage . Hage is a teammate of current Red Wings prospect JP Hurlbert at the University of Michigan. Also coming back to Detroit in the trade are conditional first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, a 2027 second-round pick, and a 2028 fourth-rounder. While the Canadiens were not on Larkin’s official 10-team trade list, after losing over a million dollars in the three weeks since deciding he would no longer play for the Red Wings, apparently Detroit was able to convince Larkin to waive his no-trade clause to move north of the border. Packing his bags for Detroit meanwhile, Dach has been playing primarily on the Canadiens third line, with two goals and six assists so far this season while playing on a one year, 3.6 million dollar contract. Montembault is currently on injured reserve , having last played in March of this year. The 30-year-old veteran netminder has played 232 games in the NHL, primarily with the Canadiens and is signed to a 3.15 million dollar AAV contract that expires later this year. Coach Sean Payton ’s Denver Broncos are 8-2 after a 38-24 home win over the Las Vegas Raiders that saw offensive coordinator Davis Webb’s unit come to life on a day when franchise star Tom Jackson’s passing was announced, leading to a ‘Jacked Up’ ESPN tribute . The Broncos’ offense starred in the win as Jonah Coleman reached a Clinton Portis pantheon at the running back position. Following the game, Payton had a special tribute locked and loaded for Jackson. “He got a game ball tonight, his family…Part of the rich history, obviously, tough loss for everyone,” Payton said, clearly emotional over the loss of the Broncos and ESPN legend. Here’s Sean Payton on Jackson postgame 👇🏼 pic.twitter.com/xp6i4x1nUN — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 23, 2026 Jackson was a big-time playmaker with the Broncos, intercepting 20 passes and recovering eight fumbles in 14 seasons with the franchise. Denver’s Vance Joseph-led defense didn’t have its best day against the Raiders, giving up nearly 370 yards to its rookie Fernando Mendoza-led attack, but the offense picked them up. QB Bo Nix had 225 yards passing with one touchdown and one interception, while Coleman rushed for 111 yards on 24 carries with three touchdowns. The Broncos missed out on key opportunities in the first half as Troy Franklin botched a Nix deep ball that had six points written all over it. The second half was better as the Broncos cashed in their opportunities, cruising to a much-needed division win. Coach Payton and his franchise got the opportunity to learn about a true Broncos and NFL legend on Sunday, but not under the circumstances that they wanted to hear.
